basics.name: Hung-Chun Chang
basics.label: M.S. Student in Psychology, National Taiwan University
basics.summary: I study whether computational models of learners hold up against real learning data, with a focus on LLM-based simulated students, and I build the tutoring systems and social robots I run those studies in.

work.name: Master's Thesis Research (in progress), Department of Psychology, National Taiwan University
work.position: Validity of LLMs as Simulated Students
work.summary: Advisors: Prof. Hsiu-Ping Yueh, Prof. Feng-Ming Tsao, and Prof. Hiroaki Ogata (Kyoto University).
highlights: Recast the validity of an ability-conditioned LLM student simulator as a nomological network of four behavioral evidences: profile–behavior consistency, fidelity of error, boundary of competence, and stateful learning.
Tested all four concurrently against real per-tier learner data from the PSLC DataShop Fractions 2012 corpus, using zero-shot prompting and a 2×2 fine-tuning ablation (reasoning × history).

Found that fine-tuning with reasoning and history simulated students best, yet the competence paradox persisted and the learning mechanism was not reproduced; this first part was accepted at ReLEAF@ICCE 2026 (first author).

work.name: Social Lab Human-Robot Interaction Group, National Taiwan University
work.summary: Prof. Hsiu-Ping Yueh, Prof. Weijane Lin; Department of Psychology.
highlights: Designed the simulated-student evaluation for an intelligent robot tutor (Enterprise Information Systems, 2026) and the manipulation check for a robot-personality study (International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction, 2026).
Sole developer of research systems deployed with real users in a museum, a library, and with older adults.
Held 2 workshops on multimodal data analysis and voice-based social robots and 4 on social robot programming; mentored 3 undergraduate projects.

projects.name: ECRobot, a robot tutor (sole developer)
projects.summary: An intelligent tutoring system with an iPad app (Swift) for handwriting input, a NAO robot (Qi Python) as voice user interface, and a FastAPI backend. Used in a between-subjects learning study.
highlights: Instantiated prospect theory as an empathetic feedback algorithm for the robot tutor.
Designed the student simulation pipeline and evaluation method, and wrote the first draft of the paper.

projects.name: Social Robot Design Platform (initiator & sole developer)
projects.summary: A web-based end-user programming tool that implements a design language for social robot behavior, derived from developing 5 social robotic systems.
highlights: Refined with four groups of student researchers in a research-through-design process over 6 months.
Deployed in a laboratory experiment for over a month.

projects.name: TouchHear, an AR assistive learning system (sole developer)
projects.summary: Real-time fingertip tracking on a depth camera that turns printed images into touch-responsive audio surfaces for visually impaired learners.
highlights: Replaced the experimenter-in-the-loop step of the original protocol with automatic tracking.
Built an authoring interface that lets non-programmers map audio to regions of any printed image.
Designed the printed template's ArUco markers to carry both depth-plane calibration and project identity, making each sheet self-describing.

projects.name: Companion robot for older adults
highlights: Operationalized discourse affectiveness into measurable linguistic indicators and validated the manipulation with NLP-based checks.
Developed the front-end app that presents the robot's responses.
Sustained conversations averaging 15 minutes per session and 30 minutes per participant.
